Exactly enumerate rank-one and rank-two sketches, calculate the resulting exact projector losses, then apply two tight-frame identities and two Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities to prove the universal sharp expected-loss bound for every invertible real 3x3 target and every positive integer sketch width. Equality forces all four mutually nonorthogonal spanning signs to be Gram eigenvectors and therefore a scalar Gram matrix. The accompanying exact-rational checker passed 180 parameter checks and eight distribution checks; finite tests are supplemental.

value.rationale: Exact finite-sample calibration for a natural discrete sketching distribution in the first square dimension with four distinct sign lines: provides both full matrix-dependent expected Frobenius residual and sharp uniform worst-case loss for every oversampling width. Even ell=3 fails to recover rank 3 with probability 5/8; unlike Gaussian full-dimensional sketches, extra sign columns only suppress but never eliminate rank failure at finite width. Isotropic Gram matrices are the unique hardest inputs. This is not merely the elementary rank count: the weighted residual and universal extremality are proved as new mathematical content.
